location: §3.4: "The first interval is closed, which only adds the point 1, handled identically by treating [1,β] as (1-δ,β] with δ<1."
objection:
This is the only weak spot I found, and it is cosmetic. Applying the Lemma on (1-δ,β] produces the integral (1/e)∫_{1-δ}^{β}F, not (1/e)∫_1^{β}F. It also needs F to be defined and monotone on (1-δ,1). That can fail for some δ<1: for f=3t-1, f(t)<0 for t<1/3, so the square root in F is undefined there. The simple fix is to take the point k=1 out of the sum and apply the Lemma on (1,β]. This adds at most F(1)≤c_3F(y) to the error for each residue class, which the constant 6d·c_3 in (3.9) already absorbs. Alternatively, take δ small enough that f>0 and F is monotone on (1-δ,1], and bound the extra integral by sup F. Neither fix changes any exponent or constant dependence.

What I checked and found correct:
- The identities for A_p, B_p−A_p and D_p−B_p, and the bounds |B_p−A_p|<1/p, −p^{-3/2}<D_p−B_p<0 and A_p≥1/2.
- τ_p is a convex combination of A_p, B_p, D_p (using z_p≤x_p, from ρ(p²)≤pρ(p)), so τ_p>0. |τ_p−1|≤(3+2d)/p² for primes p outside P_0 (the primes dividing the content of f).
- u=b*μ, the bounds (3.1)–(3.4) (including the constant C_1 for primes in P_0), the Rankin tail bound (3.5), the short-sum bound (3.6), and the Euler product (3.7) for τ_p/A_p.
- The tail T_k, using Σ_{e|n}4^{ω(e)}≤τ(n)³ and f(k)≤Y.
- The residue-class Lemma.
- The monotonicity split: F'=P/(2√f) with deg P=2d−2 and leading coefficient a²d(3d−2).
- The assembly and the absorption of ε, with constants depending only on f and ε, uniformly for real y≥1.
- Claims (b) and (c) follow directly from (0.1).
- No post-2010 or excluded sources are used.

other_issues: §3.5: the term written O(Y^{3/2}y^{-1/2}) comes from (2/3)(Y^{3/2}−f(1)^{3/2})·O(y^{-1/2}). This is correct but only implicit; the bounded-sum O(1) term is handled correctly.
